messages:
anita: Heads-up — we're reviewing GCP Cloud KMS guidance for Private/on-prem deployments. Customer wants envelope encryption with our agent talking to their KMS. Need clear guidance on: svcacc scoping, keyring placement (host vs customer project), minimal roles, audit logging sinks, and rotation playbook. Any gotchas?

jamie: +1. Narrow questions: will our agent run in customer's network using a customer SA (recommended) or will we impersonate a host-project SA? If customer-managed SA, we should avoid granting broad roles.

marco: Prefer customer-managed SA pinned to their keyring in their project. Gives clear separation and audit trail. We can document these minimal bindings: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the specific cryptoKey, roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator only if they need to impersonate. Avoid project-level roles.

anita: Can you paste the exact IAM snippet we should recommend in the onboarding doc? Also: what about key rings vs keys lifecycle — should we ask them to create key per-tenant?

marco: Rough IAM example (customer-run):
```
# grant encrypt/decrypt for our service account on a single key
PROJECT=my-customer-project
KEYRING=redwood-keyring
KEY=my-app-kek
SA=service-account@${PROJECT}.iam.gserviceaccount.com

gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding 
  projects/${PROJECT}/locations/global/keyRings/${KEYRING}/cryptoKeys/${KEY} 
  --member=serviceAccount:${SA} 
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
```
Also add roles/logging.logWriter for agents if they emit structured logs to a customer-owned sink.

eli: Quick note on envelope encryption: we should recommend CEKs generated per-file/request and encrypted with the KEK (KMS key). Avoid long-lived CEKs in memory/persisted storage. If agent uses local disk cache, always rotate CEKs on cache eviction.

ops-oncall: Audit/logging: enable Data Access audit logs for the KMS key at the project level so Cloud Audit Logs capture Encrypt/Decrypt calls. Create a log sink to the customer's BigQuery or a customer-managed GCS bucket for retention. Also suggest an alert on unusual Decrypt volumes (e.g., > 3x baseline in 5m).

security-bot: Checklist to include in onboarding manifest: 
- KMS key location (region/global)
- Key rotation schedule and who controls it
- Service account email we will use
- CryptoKey IAM binding (encrypter/decrypter)
- Audit log export destination + retention
- Emergency re-wrap contact + process

anita: Rotation playbook question: if customer rotates KEK frequently, what should our agent support to avoid downtime?

jamie: Support both graceful re-wrap and parallel keys. Options:
- Preferred: customer uses KMS key versioning and rotates by creating a new key version and marking it as primary. Agent should fetch the latest key version for new CEK wraps, and keep a short cache of previous versions for decrypting existing CEKs.
- Fallback: re-wrap flow — agent receives a notification (pub/sub) and performs re-wrap (decrypt with old, encrypt with new) for cached CEKs.

marco: Implementation detail: use KMS API's decrypt which automatically works for older versions if allowed. For re-wrap at scale avoid decrypt-encrypt hotspots — do in background batches with rate limits and backoff.

eli: Also call out KMS request quotas and latency — avoid using KMS for every tokenized operation. Batch CEK generation, use prefix/KV caches and local CEK caches with TTLs. Provide recommended TTLs (e.g., CEK TTL 15–60s for very latency-sensitive flows, up to 5m for background tasks).

anita: Good. Any RBAC pitfalls we should warn customers about?

marco: A few:
- Don’t grant cloudkms.admin to our SA. Too broad.
- Avoid project-owner bindings; scope to the specific cryptoKey resource.
- If using cross-project service accounts, set up iam.serviceAccountUser carefully and grant only impersonation where strictly needed.
- Watch out for "allUsers" or "allAuthenticatedUsers" on key bindings — never acceptable.

ops-oncall: Additional ops tip: create a dedicated key for production workloads and separate keys for staging + dev. Label keys with environment and contact info. Ensure key rotation logs are retained for at least 13 months for compliance.

anita: Can someone draft a short onboarding snippet we can drop into the Private deployment runbook for customers? I can convert to a checklist.

marco: I'll sketch it and push to the runbook repo today — will include the IAM example, audit sink example, rotation options, and the re-wrap runbook. cc @jamie @eli for review.

jamie: Thanks — also let's add a small troubleshooting section: common errors like PERMISSION_DENIED (missing encrypter role), KEY_NOT_FOUND (wrong key path), QUOTA_EXCEEDED (too many decrypts) and recommended remediation steps.

anita: Perfect. If we all agree, I'll mark this thread as the canonical eng-security reference for KMS Private onboarding and link the runbook when available. :+1:

security-bot: Incident note: logged as security:KMS-ONPREM-2026-01 for tracking onboarding improvements.
